newsitem.title: USA: NBA-ROCKETS' OLAJUWON RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL.
newsitem.headline: NBA-ROCKETS' OLAJUWON RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL.

text.p: Houston Rockets centre Hakeem Olajuwon was released from hospital Monday after doctors shocked his heart back into a normal rhythm.
Team officials said Olajuwon would miss a Monday night game against the Toronto Raptors, but was expected to return to the court in a few days.

Olajuwon, 33, was admitted to Methodist Hospital Sunday after suffering an irregular heartbeat for the second time in less than two weeks. He reported the problem at halftime of a game Saturday night against the Washington Bullets, but continued to play after a team trainer gave his approval.
Team physician James Muntz told reporters that Olajuwon's heart was given an electric shock Monday morning to restore a normal heartbeat.
"He responded immediately with one treatment and he's back in a regular heart rhythm," he said.
Olajuwon told reporters as he walked out of the hospital that he felt fine and had been given medication for the arrhythmia.
"I have a very good heart so there's really no major concern. It's just something I'll have to learn to live with," he said.

Olajuwon was hospitalized for two days on November 19 after he suffered arrhythmia at halftime of a game against the Minnesota Timberwolves. His heart had to be shocked back into a normal rhythm during that episode, too.
In 1991, Olajuwon missed seven games because of an irregular heartbeat. Despite the periodic occurrences, physicians said the problem was not a threat to his basketball career or his life.

"This is a benign rhythm. It's uncomfortable for him because your heart's going fast, but at no point would the Rockets or any of the doctors let him play if this was something dangerous," Muntz said.
His heart problems notwithstanding, Olajuwon scored 34 points and pulled down 17 rebounds against Washington Saturday to lead the Rockets to a 103-99 victory.

The Nigerian-born U.S. citizen was a member of the U.S. gold-medal Dream Team in the Summer Olympics in Atlanta and led the Rockets to NBA championships in 1994 and 1995. He is an 11-time All-Star who won the league's Most Valuable Player Award in 1994.
